processing.reason: No source-grounded original/transformed program pair can be validated for this PR. The historical change is not a program-MIR value rewrite: it adds an early `Err("still needs substitution")` in `check_mir_is_available` for `InstanceDef::DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` when `ty` still has `TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PARAM`. The bad behavior was eager drop-shim instance/MIR resolution in the inliner, which could trigger a `ConstParamHasTy`/query-cycle compiler ICE; the fix merely stalls inlining. The PR's regression test (`tests/ui/const-generics/polymorphic-drop-shim.rs`) is build-pass only and asserts successful compilation, not runtime output. The frozen analysis likewise states this is an instance-resolution precondition, not a wrong rewrite of program MIR. Therefore there is no justified pair of ordinary Rust functions whose defined Miri executions should produce different numeric/boolean/character values under the fixed modern compiler. Constructing such a pair would require manufacturing an unrelated eager-vs-delayed drop semantics change, which the PR evidence does not support.

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/inline.rs`, `check_mir_is_available` screened instance kinds before allowing the inliner to obtain callee MIR. `InstanceDef::Intrinsic(_) | InstanceDef::Virtual(..)` were rejected as `"instance without MIR (intrinsic / virtual)"`, while the default path accepted shim instances with the comment: `"This cannot result in an immediate cycle since the callee MIR is a shim, which does not get any optimizations run on it."` A `DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` instance therefore fell through to the shim/default path even when its type still contained unsubstituted const generics.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was to let MIR inlining proceed with a drop-shim instance whose dropped type still contained unsubstituted const parameters: `InstanceDef::DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` with `ty.has_type_flags(TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PARAM)` was treated as available shim MIR. This prematurely resolved/instantiated the drop shim before its const params were substituted, interacting badly with `ConstParamHasTy` in the drop-shim builder. The correction is to stall, returning `Err("still needs substitution")`, until all const params of the drop-glue type are substituted. This is not a wrong rewrite of program MIR; it is an incorrect instance-resolution precondition in the inliner.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR inlining (`-Zinline-mir=yes`) of polymorphic Rust code where an inline/generic function calls `std::ptr::drop_in_place` on a pointee type containing a const-generic parameter, and the drop glue instance still has an unsubstituted const parameter at the point where the inliner queries callee MIR. The regression test uses `pub struct Foo<T, const N: usize>([T; N]);`, a `Drop` type `Dorp`, and `#[inline] pub unsafe fn drop<const M: usize>(x: *mut Foo<Dorp, M>)`.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix in MIR inlining: the inliner must not resolve a drop-shim instance (`DropGlue(_, Some(ty))`) while its type still contains unsubstituted const parameters. It must stall with "still needs substitution" because the drop-shim builder does not evaluate predicates in the correct param-env; otherwise inlining a function that drops a const-generic-parameterized type can trigger `ConstParamHasTy` problems. The included regression test is a build-pass test with `-Zinline-mir=yes`.
analysis.trigger: Inlining is enabled and the inliner considers a `DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` instance where `ty` has `TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PARAM`, e.g. an `#[inline]` generic function with a const parameter that calls `std::ptr::drop_in_place` on `*mut Foo<Dorp, M>` with `M` not yet substituted.
preconditions: MIR inlining is active (regression test uses `-Zinline-mir=yes`).
The code contains a polymorphic function with an unsubstituted const-generic parameter.
That function drops a value whose type contains the const parameter, producing a `DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` instance with `HAS_CT_PARAM` still set.
Const params must not be assumed substituted merely because the instance is drop glue/shim MIR.
pitfalls: Do not treat all shim/drop-glue MIR as immediately available: drop shims can still need const-generic substitution.
The issue concerns an unsubstituted const parameter (`HAS_CT_PARAM`), not merely any generic parameter; a guard on all generics would be broader than the historical fix.
The bad interaction is with the drop-shim builder's param-env (`ConstParamHasTy`), so resolving the shim eagerly is the mistake, not the subsequent inlining decisions.
This patch bundle also contains feature-gating, lint-default, CI URL, and LLVM-submodule changes; those do not establish inliner behavior and should not be conflated with this optimization fix.
The test is build-pass only; no compiler was built or executed for this analysis, so do not claim observed reproduction or runtime behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a build-pass UI test under `tests/ui/const-generics/` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir=yes --crate-type=lib`. Define a const-generic struct whose element has a `Drop` impl, then define an `#[inline]` function with its own const parameter that calls `std::ptr::drop_in_place` on a raw pointer to that instantiated type. The test differentiator is whether the drop-glue type still contains an unsubstituted const parameter when the inliner queries MIR: a monomorphic/concrete const instantiation should remain compilable, while the generic const-param case must be stalled rather than resolving the drop shim early. Assert successful compilation (no ICE), not runtime output.
